verses.text: Now these are those who came to David to Ziklag, while he was a fugitive from Saul the son of Kish. They were among the mighty men, his helpers in war.
They were armed with bows, and could use both the right hand and the left in slinging stones and in shooting arrows from the bow. They were of Saul’s relatives of the tribe of Benjamin.
The chief was Ahiezer, then Joash, the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; Jeziel and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth; Beracah; Jehu the Anathothite;
Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the thirty and a leader of the thirty; Jeremiah; Jahaziel; Johanan; Jozabad the Gederathite;
Eluzai; Jerimoth; Bealiah; Shemariah; Shephatiah the Haruphite;
Elkanah, Isshiah Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites;
and Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.

Some Gadites joined David in the stronghold in the wilderness, mighty men of valor, men trained for war, who could handle shield and spear; whose faces were like the faces of lions, and they were as swift as the gazelles on the mountains:
Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,
Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,
Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,
Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,
Jeremiah the tenth, and Machbannai the eleventh.
These of the sons of Gad were captains of the army: he who was least was equal to one hundred, and the greatest to one thousand.
These are those who went over the Jordan in the first month, when it had overflowed all its banks; and they put to flight all who lived in the valleys, both toward the east and toward the west.
Some of the children of Benjamin and Judah came to the stronghold to David.

David went out to meet them, and answered them, “If you have come peaceably to me to help me, my heart will be united with you; but if you have come to betray me to my adversaries, since there is no wrong in my hands, may the God of our fathers see this and rebuke it.”

Then the Spirit came on Amasai, who was chief of the thirty, and he said, “We are yours, David, and on your side, you son of Jesse. Peace, peace be to you, and peace be to your helpers; for your God helps you.” Then David received them, and made them captains of the band.

Some of Manasseh also joined David, when he came with the Philistines against Saul to battle; but they didn’t help them; for the lords of the Philistines sent him away after consultation, saying, “He will desert to his master Saul to the jeopardy of our heads.”
As he went to Ziklag, some from Manasseh joined him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai, captains of thousands who were of Manasseh.
They helped David against the band of rovers; for they were all mighty men of valor, and were captains in the army.
For from day to day men came to David to help him, until there was a great army, like God’s army.
These are the numbers of the heads of those who were armed for war, who came to David to Hebron, to turn the kingdom of Saul to him, according to Yahweh’s word.
The children of Judah who bore shield and spear were six thousand eight hundred, armed for war.
Of the children of Simeon, mighty men of valor for the war, seven thousand one hundred.
Of the children of Levi four thousand six hundred.
Jehoiada was the leader of the household of Aaron; and with him were three thousand seven hundred,
and Zadok, a young man mighty of valor, and of his father’s house twenty-two captains.
Of the children of Benjamin, Saul’s relatives, three thousand: for until then, the greatest part of them had kept their allegiance to Saul’s house.
Of the children of Ephraim twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty men of valor, famous men in their fathers’ houses.
Of the half-tribe of Manasseh eighteen thousand, who were mentioned by name, to come and make David king.
Of the children of Issachar, men who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do, their heads were two hundred; and all their brothers were at their command.
Of Zebulun, such as were able to go out in the army, who could set the battle in array, with all kinds of instruments of war, fifty thousand, and who could command and were not of double heart.
Of Naphtali one thousand captains, and with them with shield and spear thirty-seven thousand.
Of the Danites who could set the battle in array, twenty-eight thousand six hundred.
Of Asher, such as were able to go out in the army, who could set the battle in array, forty thousand.
On the other side of the Jordan, of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and of the half-tribe of Manasseh, with all kinds of instruments of war for the battle, one hundred twenty thousand.

All these were men of war, who could order the battle array, and came with a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel; and all the rest also of Israel were of one heart to make David king.
They were there with David three days, eating and drinking; for their brothers had supplied provisions for them.

Moreover those who were near to them, as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought bread on donkeys, on camels, on mules, and on oxen: supplies of flour, cakes of figs, clusters of raisins, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep in abundance; for there was joy in Israel.

footnotes.content: David was hunted, living as a fugitive—and yet men of valor came to him. I've noticed how the Lord draws faithful hearts to His own, even when everything looks defeated. These mighty warriors saw in David what the world couldn't see yet.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ambidextrous warriors—skilled with both hands in slinging and archery. They came from Benjamin, Saul's own tribe, yet chose to leave a king to follow a fugitive. Such skill was rare; rarer still was the loyalty that left tribe and honor for an uncertain promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ahiezer led the list. These names—Gibeathite, Azmaveth's sons—were rooted in towns and families. Yet they uprooted themselves to answer David's call. The Lord often calls us away from what is comfortable to stand beside His chosen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ishmaiah stood among the thirty as a leader of leaders. The text marks his rank plainly—not boasting, just counting. Sometimes the Lord simply places faithful ones in their proper place, and the rest follows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: More names, more men willing to risk everything. I've learned that the Kingdom of God advances not by the fame of a few, but by the quiet courage of many unknown hearts. Each name here matters to the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Korahites—descendants of Korah, a man whose rebellion once shook Israel. Yet here his children come to David, choosing allegiance instead. The Lord's grace reaches into family lines, turning descendants from rebellion toward obedience.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joelah and Zebadiah from Gedor—two more names, two more lives surrendered. The record keeps naming them. Even now, centuries later, their choice to follow the Lord's anointed is written down and remembered. Nothing done for Him is ever lost.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Gadites came—mighty men with faces like lions, swift as gazelles. These describers of strength echo the valor of warriors like David himself. Yet they brought their gifts to serve, not to rule. The strongest find their true calling in loyalty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ezer was chief, Obadiah second, Eliab third—a chain of command ready made. The Gadites arrived already organized, already unified. Sometimes the Lord brings us help that is not just capable but also rightly ordered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mishmannah fourth, Jeremiah fifth. The list continues, each man ranked, each important. There's something about how the Spirit honors even those we've never heard of by writing their names in Scripture.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh. The naming goes on—eleven captains of Gad, each one remembered. I'm struck by how the Lord's book never forgets the faithful, however small their shadow on the world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Johanan eighth, Elzabad ninth. The roster fills—warriors standing in order. There's a quiet dignity in how these names are kept, not for earthly fame but for the record of the King.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah tenth, Machbannai eleventh—the roster of Gad completes at eleven. Even the numbering itself becomes a kind of worship, a witness to the completeness of what the Lord gathered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The least of them matched one hundred in battle; the greatest matched a thousand. This ratio—a tenfold span in one company—speaks to true martial skill: even the humblest warrior was mighty. The Lord gathers not the weak, but the willing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They crossed the Jordan in flood, overcame all resistance, and scattered armies in every direction. The Lord often tests His own by water and danger. These men passed through—not around—the rising tide, and the Lord made them victorious.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Benjamin and Judah came to David at the stronghold. Saul's tribe and the tribe of Judah—two peoples who might have clashed instead came united to the Lord's anointed. His peace precedes His kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David tests their hearts: "Come to help, and we are one; come to betray, and God will judge." There's both welcome and warning here—the heart of a true leader. He opens himself but guards his conscience in the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Spirit came upon Amasai, and he spoke: "We are yours, David." Here is a real anchor—the work of the Holy Spirit confirming loyalty. When the Spirit moves on a man's heart to speak truth, all doubt dissolves. David received them at once.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Some from Manasseh came with David when he walked among the Philistines, yet didn't fight Saul. They wavered—stood in a hard place, caught between two kings. Sometimes faithfulness means not acting, knowing the Lord's time has not come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Later, at Ziklag, these Manassites joined David—Adnah, Jozabad, and the rest, now captains of thousands. The Lord gave them a second chance to commit fully. How gracious He is to those who stumble into His will.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They proved themselves mighty men of valor, fighting raiders and taking their place as army captains. The Lord often tests what we say we believe by asking us to prove it in battle. Their later faithfulness was the truest answer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Day by day, men came to David until his band became an army—God's army. I've learned that the Kingdom grows not by the power of one, but by the daily faithfulness of many. Each person who comes changes everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: These armed men came to Hebron to make David king—not by conquest, but according to the Lord's word. When God's word is known, a whole people can move in one direction. The King's claim was written on their hearts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Judah brought six thousand eight hundred warriors, armed and ready. The numbers begin to mount—each tribe counting its strength and laying it at David's feet. Submission to the true king looks like offering everything we have.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Simeon sent seven thousand one hundred mighty men of valor. Each tribe heard the call and answered—not because David forced them, but because they knew in their souls this was the Lord's will.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Levi came with four thousand six hundred. Even the priestly tribe laid down their robes to stand in the assembly. The work of worship and the work of kingdom are one.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehoiada, leader of Aaron's household, brought three thousand seven hundred—a real anchor in Israel's priesthood structure. The priestly line recognized and served the Lord's anointed king. Authority in God's house flows from one head.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zadok, young and mighty, brought twenty-two captains from his father's house. I'm moved by how the young rise to serve—not waiting for permission or age, but stepping forward when the Lord calls.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Benjamin—Saul's own tribe—sent three thousand, though many had kept faith with Saul's house until this hour. The shift was real; they felt it as a turning point. The Lord's time finally came, and they recognized it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ephraim brought twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty men famous in their fathers' houses. The great tribes moved—not small or reluctant, but with their full strength and their best names.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Half of Manasseh sent eighteen thousand, all named and called out to make David king. The calling of names was itself a command—an identity that pointed toward obedience. When the Lord speaks our name, we know what He wants.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Issachar sent two hundred heads with an unusual gift—"men who understood the times, who knew what Israel ought to do." This is wisdom itself: the ability to read the hour and counsel what is right. Discernment is as precious as swords.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zebulun sent fifty thousand battle-ready, not of double heart. "Double heart" means divided loyalty—but these came whole. The Lord treasures those who hold nothing back, whose yes is yes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Naphtali sent a thousand captains with thirty-seven thousand armed men. Officers and soldiers in right proportion—a tribe that came not just strong but organized, ready to serve under David's command.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dan sent twenty-eight thousand six hundred, ready to set the battle array. Each tribe brought not just numbers but skill—the fruit of years of watching and training for such a moment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Asher sent forty thousand able to go to war. The tribes kept coming—each one heard the same call and answered the same way. The unity was not demanded but freely given.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: East of Jordan, Reuben, Gad, and half Manasseh sent one hundred twenty thousand, fully equipped. Even those distant came—the Lord's call reached across water and wilderness. Distance is no barrier to obedience.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All of them came with perfect heart to Hebron to make David king—not divided, not grudging, but whole. The text says "all the rest also of Israel were of one heart." I've learned that when God's time comes, His people simply know.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They stayed three days with David, eating and drinking, celebrating together. The brothers had prepared provisions—everyone shared in the joy. Covenant is sealed not just by words but by bread and peace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this abundance—flour, figs, raisins, oil, cattle, sheep—brought by those near and far. Even now, when the Lord calls, His people still supply one another. The joy that filled Israel then still fills us when we gather in His name. As of 2026-10, I'm grateful that the same Spirit that moved those ancient hearts still moves ours toward unity and generosity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
